rationale: The record clearly addresses urban household water supply access (C1), tariff/pricing design and administrative simplicity mechanisms (C2 narrow and plain), and affordability for poor customers (C4). However, the abstract frames the study as a 'typology of water pricing options' supported by a 'review of theoretical insights and empirical experiences,' leaving unclear whether it conducts a systematic empirical synthesis or primary/secondary empirical evaluation versus an unsystematic narrative/conceptual review (C3). Under Phase 5 rules against premature exclusion of tariff/affordability studies, full-text inspection is required ('unsure').
plain_vs_narrow_note: No divergence between narrow and plain Criterion 2: urban water pricing/tariff options and administrative simplicity squarely satisfy both the narrow tariff/cost-recovery/subsidy mechanism reading and the plain regulatory/administrative reading. Both decisions are 'unsure' solely because Criterion 3 (whether the 'review of theoretical insights and empirical experiences' constitutes a systematic empirical synthesis or includes eligible primary/secondary empirical analysis rather than a narrative conceptual review) requires full-text verification.

evidence_quotes.quote: An important criterion for the design of urban water prices is the affordability of water supply for poor customers.
This paper presents a typology of water pricing options which policy-makers have at their disposal in order to address affordability.

A review of theoretical insights and empirical experiences reveals, however, how the real-world performance of these options depends on the characteristics of their technological and socio-economic environment.
